messages.author: 609a03d9f9c9c02f
messages.subject: complex mediation model
parts:
Hello,
I have a fairly complex mediation model (multilevel mediated moderation with categorical/nominal exogenous variables) and I want to ensure I am setting it up correctly.

At a high level, I want to know if differences in several beliefs help account for (mediate) why people of different political orientations have different moral judgments of various statements.
 
The actual study is setup as follows:
Participants rate a random 20/40 possible statements on: how immoral they are ('immoral'), and several other beliefs related to the statements ('disadvantage.sc' and 'freq.sc' in this example) -- these are all continuous variables.
Each participant also reports their political orientation ('pol.c' here) - again, a continuous variable.
For this example, I cut the dataset down to only 3 out of the 40 statements to simplify. 
Because statement is a categorical variable, I created two dummy variables ('s1' and 's2') to capture the statement effect, and then multiplied these by the political orientation score to create two dummy interaction variables ('polXs1' and 'polXs2')

An image of the head of the dataset is attached.


In doing some regression models, morality judgments depend on the interaction of political orientation and statement. The other beliefs ('disadvantage.sc' and 'freq.sc') also depend on the interaction of political orientation and statement. 

I want to know if these other beliefs mediate this interaction's effects on moral judgments. I don't care about differences between statements, or differences between beliefs. I just want a single test of whether considering these beliefs helps mediate these effects (e.g. so I can say that if you accounted for all these belief differences, people of different political orientations would have more similar moral judgments).

Here is my model.

lavMed <- '
level: 1
  # direct effect on moral judgements (interaction is effect of interest, main effects there to control for them)
  immoral ~ pol.c + s1 + s2 + c1*polXs1 + c2*polXs2
 
  # mediators - the two other beliefs (interaction is effect of interest, main effects there to control for them)
  disadvantage.sc ~ pol.c + s1 + s2 + dis_a1*polXs1 + dis_a2*polXs2
  freq.sc ~ pol.c + s1 + s2 + freq_a1*polXs1 + freq_a2*polXs2

  #mediators predicting outcome
  immoral ~ dis_b*disadvantage.sc + freq_b*freq.sc

  # total indirect effect (a*b) for each statement dummy code, summed over all mediators
  tot_ab1 := dis_a1*dis_b + freq_a1*freq_b
  tot_ab2 := dis_a2*dis_b + freq_a2*freq_b
 
  # total effect (total effect of interaction of politics and statement, for each statement dummy code)
  total1 := c1 + tot_ab1
  total2 := c2 + tot_ab2

level: 2
#I don't have a level 2 model in mind, so I put a saturated model here. (I set this up as a multilevel model to account for the equivalent of random intercepts for each participant.)
  immoral ~~ immoral + disadvantage.sc + freq.sc
  disadvantage.sc ~~ disadvantage.sc + freq.sc
  freq.sc ~~ freq.sc
'

fit <- sem(lavMed,
           data = d_tmp,
           cluster = "ResponseId")
summary(fit)

#omnibus test over the indirect effects. (I want a single test of if, in any case, the indirect effects are different than 0. I.e. does accounting for beliefs ever help explain political differences in moral judgments?)
con = '
   tot_ab1 == 0
   tot_ab2 == 0
'
lavTestWald(fit, constraints = con)


Some things I am not sure about:
-Political orientation is technically a level 2 variable, though I am only including the main effect of politics to control for it. Is it fine to put it where I have it in the level 1 model and not in the level 2 model?

-Is the omnibus test on my indirect effects the correct way to test my conceptual question and get a single value for the indirect effects being significant or not?

Aside from this, is there anything else I got incorrect?

Any feedback would be much appreciated!
Thalia

messages.author: 609a03d9f9c9c02f
messages.subject: Re: complex mediation model
parts:
After running this model and getting several warnings (no variance within several clusters for some of the variables, and it not liking that I put political orientation as a level 1 variable), I have adjusted the model to run as a single-level model, and just included cluster = ResponseId when fitting it to get cluster-robust SEs. 

If anyone could confirm that this updated model and my omnibus tests on it are reasonable, that would still be appreciated!
